core_obligations: Write down the identification of the localised Tor modules at a prime of the tensor product (proof lines 15121-15125).
Derive that the second condition implies the third (proof lines 15126-15127).
Use local testing of vanishing to derive Tor independence from the third condition (proof lines 15128-15130).
Derive the second condition from Tor independence by the same identification (proof lines 15131-15141).
proof_roadmap: (2) implies (3), and (3) implies (1) by local testing (proof lines 15126-15130).
(1) implies (2) by the same identification (proof lines 15131-15141).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises Tor independence of two algebras over a ring by the local Tor independence of their localisations at primes lying over a common prime of the base, and by vanishing of the localised Tor modules at every prime of the tensor product. The proof is short and consists of identifying the localised Tor modules with the Tor modules of the localisations using the standing localisation result for Tor, reading off one implication directly from that identity, using the fact that vanishing of a module can be tested at primes for the implication from the local vanishing to global Tor independence, and applying the same identification in the other direction.
